items.title: SCH-001 sits under ALL TWELVE kernels: the v0.1 preregistration schema cannot satisfy RESEARCH-METHOD.md, and every kernel's next step runs through the v0.2 migration
items.hypothesis: A single bounded migration run (v0.1 -> v0.2 for KL-001..KL-011, following KL-000's precedent) removes the one blocker that appears in every kernel's blockers list and unblocks every future preregistration at once.
items.discriminatingTest: audit_preregistrations.py reports zero schema-completeness failures across all twelve kernels.
items.whyItMatters: OPERATOR-IDENTIFIED at RUN-6 review as the most consequential thing that run touched, and until this file it was a passing mention in blockers lists. Both of RUN-6's tasks ran into it: KL-011's genuine remainder starts with its v0.2 preregistration, and KL-001's real first gate ends with one. Eleven kernels cannot leave seeded without it. It has been open since RUN-20260807-1 (SCH-001) with a known fix and a known precedent.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Converts eleven kernels from schema-blocked to work-blocked -- the difference between 'cannot register properly' and 'has not done the work'.
items.cost: one bounded run: eleven v0.2 documents populated to the standard KL-000 set; no code, no spend

items.title: The mapping pipeline is KL-001's real risk surface, and no invariant covers it
items.hypothesis: Everything KL-000 established is about ledgers already in hand. The translation INTO ledgers -- what counts as a mandatory file, what counts as searched, which scanner output becomes which root -- is where a repository result becomes right or wrong, and it currently has no registered rules, no invariants, and no ablations.
items.discriminatingTest: For every registered mapping decision, an inversion ablation caught by a registered check (the M19 discipline applied one layer up); plus the FC1-W3 scenario -- under-declared scope -- caught at the mapping layer, which is the only layer that can catch it.
items.whyItMatters: OPERATOR-IDENTIFIED. FC1 proved the evaluator sees structure only (verdict a); therefore every repository-specific failure mode lives in the mapping. Root-attribution honesty (ADV-004's near-identical-id class) and scope honesty (ADV-001) both land here. Building it without registered rules would reproduce, at KL-001, exactly the unenforced-decision defect KL-000 spent v1.3.0 repairing.
items.cost: part of KL-001's real first gate (200-400 lines plus its mapping-rule registration); not committed

items.title: The ADV-001 overlap demonstrated at FC1's E3: under-declared scope reaches a clean conclusion, in repository clothing
items.hypothesis: BL-002's mechanism (a search-space digest fixed BEFORE evidence collection) applied at the mapping layer -- the pipeline emits and commits its mandatory-file declaration before any scanning -- makes W3's silent under-declaration detectable as a declaration/reality mismatch.
items.discriminatingTest: FC1's W1/W3 pair re-run through a pipeline with prior scope commitment: W3's truncated declaration fails the commitment check instead of reaching absent_within_declared_scope.
items.whyItMatters: OPERATOR-IDENTIFIED. E3 was demonstrated on purpose and is the cheapest attack on any KL-001 result: no forgery, only omission -- and a truncated file list is also what an honest partial checkout looks like. RUN-1's BL-002 predicted this abstractly; FC1 made it concrete at the exact layer KL-001 must build. The trust boundary moves to whoever fixes the declaration; it does not disappear -- carry BL-002's honest limit forward verbatim.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether KL-001's false-clean endpoint is meaningful against a lossy or adversarial repository presenter, or only an honest one.
items.cost: one schema field + one pipeline commitment step + two fixtures, inside the KL-001 gate
items.prerequisitesNote: with BL-031; meaningless before a mapping pipeline exists
